title: Binary Number with Alternating Bits
description:
# Binary Number with Alternating Bits

Given a positive integer, check whether it has alternating bits: namely, if two adjacent bits will always have different values.

## Example 1:

**Input:** n = 5
**Output:** true
**Explanation:** The binary representation of 5 is: 101

## Example 2:

**Input:** n = 7
**Output:** false
**Explanation:** The binary representation of 7 is: 111.

## Example 3:

**Input:** n = 11
**Output:** false
**Explanation:** The binary representation of 11 is: 1011.

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= n <= 2^31 - 1`

solutions.name: Bit Trick
solutions.description: If n has alternating bits, then n XOR (n >> 1) produces all 1s. Check if that result is a power of 2 minus 1 (i.e., m & (m+1) == 0).

solutions.name: Iterative Bit Check
solutions.description: Check each pair of adjacent bits by comparing the last bit with the second-to-last bit. Shift right each iteration.
